notes: **Item R2 of the Results voice review: Ch. 2** (Identification of nutritional QTLs and candidate genes). ¶1, the GWAS model, is kept as is (your decision). This chapter is mostly facts in good order, so the changes are small: one paragraph split, one logic fix, and three sentences made unambiguous. Two of the changes also answer your open Word comments 312 and 313.
**¶2 split in two:** (counts per trait + the heritability contrast) | (strongest peaks, distribution on the chromosomes, locus size). It was one 220-word paragraph.

**4H cluster (your comment 312, "how to report this signal? As 1? Or 2?"):** report it as the locus definition produced it, two loci. That matches the count of 11 β-glucan loci, Fig. 2 and Online Resource 1. The text says in eight words why one cluster became two: "which the 50-kb gap rule split into two adjacent loci" (the gap between the two loci is 60.5 kb).

**1H fiber loci (your comment 313, "seems in the GWAS like 2 signals and reported as 6"):** likewise keep 6, and add where they sit: "five of them in two clusters (329.7–330.7 Mb and 440.0–440.6 Mb)". The reader then sees the two signals without the count changing.
**¶3 logic:** "The direction of the allelic effects was consistent within traits" was followed by the two protein loci having opposite effects. It now says it for β-glucan, fiber and starch.
**¶4:** the 1H sentence ("a third fiber locus 532 kb upstream of the nearer one") and the β-glucan sentence ("the nearest one was located 6.0 Mb away") now name what they refer to. Same numbers.
**Unchanged:** ¶1 and ¶5, all numbers, and your comments (309, 311–316 stay attached; resolve them in Word when you like).
questions: **Comments 312 and 313:** are the two proposed wordings ("which the 50-kb gap rule split into two adjacent loci"; "five of them in two clusters …") the way you want to report these signals? If yes, I suggest you resolve comments 309, 311–313 in Word afterwards.
